questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that my destination was in an English speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really difficult for me to get enrolled at UCL. I had to call them many times to get them to send an acceptance letter. I almost gave up in the end. It is really difficult to get in contact with someone at UCL who can help you and their response time is awfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a tutor/contact person when I arrived at UCL

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Since I got accepted so late at UCL I missed the deadline for applying for student housing. I had to find student housing on my own which was really difficult and extremely expensive as well. UCL could not help me find a place to live. I found a room through Facebook on a page with people renting out rooms and apartments.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more difficult to meet new people when you live on your own but the rooms and facilities might be nicer than in student accommodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult since you have 4 modules at UCL running at the same time. So you need to make sure that none of the 4 modules has timetables that clashes. Furthermore they expect you to contact each module leader to get accepted so it is not enough to register online like it is done at KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We got a handbook with modules and there is a webpage where you can check for clashes in timetables.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 1 out of the 4 modules I registered for in Denmark. Upon arrival, I had to change three of the modules because of clashes and some modules were not available anymore.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check for clashes in timetables and email every module leader from the beginning to get acceptance and to see if you have the pre-requisites

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a huge amount of modules and you can select 2 modules from any department you like. 2 of them need to be from your own home department.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level in my modules was a bit lower than at KU. Since exchange students are not there for exams you need to hand in essays at the end of term. This makes the lectures less important since you often get to pick a topic for the essays yourself.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is quite similar but mostly lectures and fewer seminars. Furthermore, I had 3 tutorials and an oral presentation during my modules where I got graded for my contribution. I am not used to getting grades during my modules and not from contribution to discussions so this was different for me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Genes and neurodegenerative diseases
Infection
Cellular pathology
Biology of ageing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked genes and neurodegenerative diseases since this was completely different from my previous modules and it had a good journal club, Infection was also a good module and the module leader is amazing, the workload is also quite small compared to my other modules.
Biology of ageing was interesting and gave a new perspective but the workload was a bit higher than my other modules with 3 tutorials and two essays to hand in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: London is a city where people eat out all the time, so you will end up spending a lot of money buying lunch every day and meeting with friends at restaurants for dinner. This was a bit surprising for me, I ended up spending most of my money on food, the food in London is great though. You can however make it cheaper if you make food yourself but people rarely do this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I spend more money on food than expected
Travel pass for underground is also quite expensive but really nice to have to get around

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Since the stay is only 3 months I did not sign up for any clubs or sports. However, if you want this there is a lot to choose from but you are probably not going to make it to many events since some clubs only meet once in a while.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have all kinds of sports clubs and food clubs, almost anything you can imagine. They even have a nordic society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the nordic society once which was fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I took weekend trips to Edinburgh, Bath, Bristol and Oxford. It is really easy to get around in the south of England by train. Some of my friends also took the train from London to Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. The culture in London is almost the same in Copenhagen. However, the city is huge so it will take some time to learn to get around and learn some of the local nice places without all the turists.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly spoke to exchange students. However, if you choose modules with tutorials or group presentations it is a nice may to speak to som elocals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved that London is such a huge city. You will never get bored in London since something new is going on all the time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you do not get student housing, go to London and stay at a hotel/hostel and find something while you are there so you can see the places, there are a lot of scammers in London.
Since there are no exams at UCL for exchange students you will have a lot of spare time to enjoy and you can manage your own time easily to make rooms for trips.
The stay is quite short since the term is only 2,5 months so it is a bit harder to make a lot of friendships but I enjoyed having a few really good friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The weather in London was a lot better than expected. Better than in Denmark during my stay.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my English, getting international friends, and getting the opportunity to live in London for a couple of months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live and to get enrolled. So mostly challenges getting settled in London. You also need to be aware that London is an expensive place to live in.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
